summary: Chunked streaming disconnects / request timeouts for very large prompt + high max_tokens
description: Issue summary: Customer reports repeated request timeouts and streaming disconnects when sending prompts with a very large prefix (~350k tokens approximate) and enabling chunked streaming with max_tokens set to 65k. Impact: Multiple API calls from LexiDocs production integration are failing (HTTP 504 / client-side disconnects). Affects document ingestion pipelines and interactive preview features. Environment: Dedicated pool (dedicated-lexidocs-east), prod us-east-1, model redwood-extended-13b pinned v2026-02-28. Observed since 2026-03-08 after customer increased their max_tokens during a content migration job.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use their client repro: POST /v1/generate with stream=true. 2) Send a single request with a prompt ~350k tokens (they provide a compressed payload; we reproduced by concatenating ~45k short paragraphs). 3) Set max_tokens=65000 and temperature=0.2. 4) Observe server sends some initial streamed chunks then stalls ~90-120s and client receives a 504 or drops connection. 5) Re-run with stream=false — request completes but with very high latency (~220s) and occasionally 504.
observed_behavior: Chunked streaming starts returning chunks but stalls mid-generation; connection either closes with 504 or the client reports socket timeout. Non-streaming completes but frequently times out at reverse-proxy or exceeds caller timeout. Token accounting appears inconsistent in some partially-completed streamed responses.
expected_behavior: Server should continue streaming until generation completes or return clear 5xx with retryable guidance. For large prefix + large max_tokens, server should either handle end-to-end within SLOs or return early with helpful error (e.g., 'request exceeds supported full-context capacity').
logs_and_traces: API Gateway request id: rq_8f7a2c3; Serving runtime trace: trace_id=trc-20260310-9a2; Router logs show long-lived backend connection kept open ~95s then an upstream 502 from proxy. Example tail from serving runtime: 'KVCache: reserve 12.3GB for prefix window; continuous-batch loop: waiting for free slot' followed by repeated 'stream-heartbeat sent' then 'connection closed by client'. Nginx proxy log excerpt shows 'upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream'.
investigation_notes: Hypotheses: 1) Continuous batching + large KV cache for extreme prefix causes starvation of kernel workers and prolongs per-request compute beyond reverse-proxy timeouts. 2) Chunked streaming flush interval interacts poorly with client-side small reads, leaving the connection open but not transferring enough bytes to keep forward proxies from timing out. 3) Edge LB/nginx default proxy_read_timeout (~90s) is being hit when generation stalls between micro-batches.
tests_run:
- Reproduced in staging (dedicated sim) using same model + payload; streaming stalled at ~100s.
- Disabled continuous batching on runtime -> streaming proceeded longer but overall latency still high and eventually hit compute limits.
- Ran with stream=false in staging -> request completed but consumed CPU/GPU for ~210s and occasionally returned 500s from scheduler under load.
- Increased proxy_read_timeout in a local gateway -> streaming completed end-to-end for one test but this is not a safe global fix.
workarounds:
- Short term: Ask customer to set stream=false for bulk migration jobs OR reduce max_tokens to <= 32k and split the prompt into smaller segments.
- Operational: If customer is on Dedicated, propose increasing reserved capacity for their pool during migrations (this temporarily reduces queuing).
- Gateway-level: Temporarily increase proxy_read_timeout for the affected dedicated pool route while we investigate (requires network/infra approval).
resolution: (pending) Engineering lead assigned to runtime and routing teams to implement a two-part mitigation: (A) make streaming heartbeats emit larger keepalive frames under high prefix loads, and (B) add explicit early-reject with actionable error when requested context+max_tokens exceeds measured safe throughput for the chosen model/instance type. Temporary proxy_read_timeout bump validated end-to-end in a canary and applied to dedicated-lexidocs-east route at 2026-03-13 18:40 UTC.
next_steps:
1) Runtime: add lightweight estimator that returns 'unsafe' for combos of prefix_length + max_tokens + model on this hardware (owner: @runtime-team, ETA 2026-03-20).
2) Router: tune streaming flush/heartbeat size and ensure chunk boundaries flush to proxy (owner: @routing-team, ETA 2026-03-18).
3) SRE: propose documented proxy timeout policy for Dedicated pools and implement temporary increased timeout for LexiDocs (owner: @sre, ETA 2026-03-14).
4) Customer success: coordinate migration schedule with LexiDocs to throttle their job or provision additional capacity (owner: @cs, contact: alice@lexidocs.com).
